titleEn: Phytoform partners with major seed breeders to bring AI-powered plant design to corn crops
titleZh: Phytoform与两大种子公司合作，用AI设计玉米植株结构
summaryZh: 英国基因编辑初创公司Phytoform与Beck's Hybrids和RAGT合作，利用其AI平台CRE.AI.TIVE优化玉米遗传性状，重点改善植株结构以提高产量和抗逆性。该技术通过机器学习识别DNA微小变化，无需外源DNA即可精准调控基因表达，旨在应对气候变化导致的玉米减产（每升温1°C减产7.4%）、病害压力增加及生产成本上升等挑战。合作将进行田间验证，并计划拓展至美国、南美和欧洲市场。
featuredReason: 该新闻展示了AI与基因编辑在玉米育种中的前沿应用，直接回应了气候变化下作物产量下降的紧迫问题，对智慧种植业从业者理解未来作物设计方向具有重要参考价值。
contentFull:
UK-based gene editing startup Phytoform is working with two of the world’s major seed companies—Beck’s Hybrids, the largest family-owned seed retailer in the US, and international breeder RAGT—to improve corn genetics for growers.

The companies will target “whole-plant corn architecture” to improve harvestable yield and productivity. While the specific trait remains undisclosed, Phytoform cofounder and CEO William Pelton describes the goal as improving how the plant grows and performs at a structural level.

Corn is the world’s most-produced cereal crop, underpinning everything from animal feed to fuel to food staples. Improving yield efficiency and plant architecture is increasingly more a necessity than a “nice to have” feature in crops. Research shows that every 1°C of warming to the planet reduces maize yields by roughly 7.4%, and some studies project losses of up to 28% by the end of the century even under optimistic adaptation scenarios.

Meanwhile, disease pressure is increasing for corn crops, production costs have roughly doubled since 2007, and the gap between potential and actual yields continues to widen. Plant architecture design such as Phytoform’s could in theory help crops do everything from capturing more light to using nitrogen more efficiently, in addition to tolerating climate stressors.

Image credit: Phytoform Labs
Complimenting, not replacing, seed breeding

The partnership combines Phytoform’s AI-powered crop development platform CRE.AI.TIVE with corn-breeding expertise from Beck’s and RAGT’s corn breeding expertise, proprietary germ plasm, and commercial market insights, says Pelton. 

Phytoform’s CRE.AI.TIVE platform employs machine learning to identify small changes to DNA sequences in plants that could bring beneficial impacts if activated. It introduces these minimal changes to the plant without the need of foreign DNA.

Targeting native gene expression gives breeders a powerful way to address agronomic challenges in corn while allowing them to work within existing elite germplasm, he adds.

Both companies have their own genetics and breed plants, which Pelton says is important, as Phytoform’s technology isn’t meant to replace breeding.

“We work with breeders to accelerate their approach to specific challenges like plant architecture. They have the channels to market, they have breeding material, and they are providing some funding.

“The technology we are effectively designing with them is DNA sequences to change the activity of a target gene, so we can fine tune it for the output they need.”

Validating AI in ‘the real world’

The partnership will also work on validation to test Phytoform’s AI output in the real world, he says.

“People make many claims about AI, and it’s a bit of a buzzword, but honestly, we are not at the point where you can take something from an AI model and transfer it straight into the field and it works first time. You have to do some level of biological validation.”

Post validation, Phytoform will supply Beck’s and RAGT with edited material they can put into their breeding germplasm and take to market.

To start, the partnership will target major agricultural markets including the United States, South America, and potentially Europe. Both Beck’s and RAGT work across millions of acres, with Beck’s primarily focused on the Midwest corn belt in the US, and RAGT in about 50 different countries.

Pelton suggests the partnership is also an opportunity to make its AI tech more available to the wider seed industry, and that this is one of the first examples of this type of technology being used outside of major ag corporates.

Crop-agnostic gene editing

Phytoform landed $4 million earlier this year to use its technology for tomatoes, and also has a corn partnership in place with Corteva.

Since Phytoform’s CRE.AI.TIVE platform is crop-agnostic, there are future opportunities to apply the technology across additional species and trait challenges, according to the company.

“The thing that makes Phytoform unique is that we’re not just a gene discovery platform,” says Pelton. “We’re not finding genes and then using gene editing to put those genes into other plants or to delete those genes or whatever.”

This also allows breeders using the company’s gene-editing tech to bypass GMO regulations, potentially carving out a faster path to market.

translationZh:
英国基因编辑初创公司Phytoform正与全球两家主要种子公司——美国最大的家族种子零售商Beck's Hybrids以及国际育种公司RAGT——合作，为种植者改良玉米遗传性状。

这些公司将聚焦于“整株玉米结构”，以提高可收获产量和生产力。虽然具体性状尚未公开，但Phytoform联合创始人兼首席执行官William Pelton将目标描述为：在结构层面改善植物的生长方式和表现。

玉米是全球产量最高的谷类作物，支撑着从动物饲料到燃料再到主食的整个产业链。提高产量效率和植株结构越来越成为作物的“必需品”而非“锦上添花”的特征。研究表明，全球每升温1°C，玉米产量就会减少约7.4%；即使在最乐观的适应情景下，一些研究预测到本世纪末玉米损失可能高达28%。

与此同时，玉米作物的病害压力不断加大，生产成本自2007年以来大约翻了一番，潜在产量与实际产量之间的差距持续扩大。像Phytoform这样的植株结构设计，理论上可以帮助作物在耐受气候胁迫的同时，实现从捕获更多光能到更高效利用氮素等多种功能。

**补充而非替代种子育种**

Pelton表示，此次合作将Phytoform的人工智能作物开发平台CRE.AI.TIVE与Beck's和RAGT的玉米育种专长、专有种质资源以及商业市场洞察相结合。

Phytoform的CRE.AI.TIVE平台利用机器学习识别植物DNA序列中的微小变化，这些变化如果被激活，可能带来有益影响。该技术在不引入外源DNA的情况下，将这些微小变化引入植物体内。

他补充说，靶向调控内源基因表达为育种者提供了一种强有力的方式来解决玉米的农艺挑战，同时使他们能够在现有优良种质资源的基础上开展工作。

两家公司都拥有自己的遗传资源和育种材料，Pelton认为这一点很重要，因为Phytoform的技术并非旨在取代育种。

“我们与育种者合作，加速他们应对特定挑战（如植株结构）的方法。他们拥有市场渠道、育种材料，并提供部分资金。

“我们与他们共同设计的技术，本质上是改变目标基因活性的DNA序列，这样我们就可以根据他们所需的产出进行微调。”

**在“现实世界”验证AI**

Pelton表示，此次合作还将进行验证工作，以测试Phytoform的AI输出在现实世界中的表现。

“人们对AI有很多说法，它有点像一个流行词，但老实说，我们还没有达到能够直接从AI模型中拿出结果并直接应用到田间、且一次就能成功的程度。你必须进行一定程度的生物学验证。”

验证完成后，Phytoform将向Beck's和RAGT提供经过编辑的材料，这些材料可以融入它们的育种种质资源中并推向市场。

初期，合作将瞄准美国、南美以及可能包括欧洲在内的主要农业市场。Beck's和RAGT的业务覆盖数百万英亩土地，其中Beck's主要专注于美国中西部玉米带，RAGT则活跃在大约50个国家。

Pelton认为，此次合作也是一个机会，可以让其AI技术更广泛地应用于整个种子行业，并且这是此类技术首次在大型农业企业之外得到应用的案例之一。

**作物无关的基因编辑**

Phytoform今年早些时候获得了400万美元资金，用于将其技术应用于番茄，并且还与科迪华（Corteva）建立了玉米合作关系。

据该公司称，由于Phytoform的CRE.AI.TIVE平台与作物种类无关，未来有机会将该技术应用于更多物种和性状挑战。

“Phytoform的独特之处在于，我们不仅仅是一个基因发现平台，”Pelton说。“我们不是发现基因，然后利用基因编辑将这些基因导入其他植物，或者删除这些基因等等。”

这也使得使用该公司基因编辑技术的育种者能够绕过转基因（GMO）法规，从而可能开辟一条更快的上市路径。
author: Jennifer Marston
